topic: The quote you sent that nobody chased. Teaching the follow-up gap.

slides.subtitle: (be honest about the answer)
slides.scene: A single white printed estimate sheet lies face up on a work truck dashboard in daylight, one corner curled, a set of van keys resting on top of it. Nothing else on the dash.
Five identical white estimate sheets stand upright in a wire rack on a workbench. Four are dulled and dusty; the nearest one is crisp and clean.
slides.annotation: nobody said no, nobody said anything
bullets: the customer did not pick someone else
they simply stopped thinking about it
one nudge would have restarted it

slides.scene: The ScaileAI field technician pushes a single solid Scaile blue message bubble forward along a thin blue line toward a small white house model on a workbench, two dim grey bubbles trailing behind it.
slides.annotation: sent while you were on a roof
bullets: a short check in beats a long pitch
ask if anything changed, not if they decided
send it before the quote goes cold

slides.scene: A paper wall calendar pinned to a garage wall, three consecutive days marked with small solid Scaile blue squares and the rest of the month left blank.
slides.annotation: a cadence, not a reminder you will ignore
bullets: a real sequence runs for weeks
it stops the moment they reply
you never touch it once it is set

slides.scene: The ScaileAI field technician holds up a white tablet showing three thick Scaile blue horizontal bands of different lengths, standing beside a matte navy toolbox on a bench.
slides.annotation: if it lives in your head it stops when you do
bullets: write the pricing rules down once
let the system apply them every time
you approve the edges, not every job

slides.scene: Two identical white estimate sheets lie side by side on a kitchen counter, one crisp and one creased and faded, a homeowner coffee mug set down on the crisp one.
slides.annotation: they had your number and your price
bullets: you did the site visit and the pricing
you just stopped talking after the send
that is the cheapest gap to close

slides.scene: The ScaileAI field technician stands beside a large white envelope propped upright on a workbench, one thick Scaile blue band across its front, one hand raised in a still wave.
slides.ctaPromise: comment it and I will send the breakdown

caption:
You did the site visit. You worked out the price. You sent the quote.

Then what.

For most contractors the honest answer is nothing. The quote goes out and every move after that belongs to the customer, who is busy, who has three other things happening, and who never actually decided against you.

That is the part worth sitting with. Most quotes do not lose to a competitor. They lose to silence.

One follow up three days later, asking whether anything has changed rather than whether they have decided, restarts more jobs than any discount will.

The reason it does not happen is not laziness. It is that you were under a sink when the reminder would have been useful, and by the evening it was gone.

I wrote up how the whole sequence works, from first response through quoting to follow up. Comment SPEED and I will send it over.
